visual.general_description: Four-panel brain MRI figure labelled A to D showing coronal, sagittal, coronal and axial views of the head at the pituitary region.
visual.detailed_description: Figure with four grayscale MRI panels in a 2 by 2 grid separated by white borders. Panel A (top left) is a coronal view with tiny green and red overlay marks at the sella. Panel B (top right) is a sagittal view with a small bright sellar structure, a short red line and a partly legible white measurement label ending in mm. Panel C (bottom left) is a darker coronal view with ruler ticks along the top. Panel D (bottom right) is an axial view with bright globes and cerebrospinal fluid. Letters A to D are printed at the left of each panel.

panels.general_description: Coronal grayscale brain MRI with black surround; the sellar region near the skull base is at the lower center with small green and red overlay marks.
panels.detailed_description: Coronal grayscale head MRI in a black frame with the printed underlined letter A at the upper left. Both cerebral hemispheres, the two lateral ventricles and the midline falx are seen above a bright skull-base region at the lower center. At the sellar level two small dark round structures lie on either side of a brighter central region. A few tiny green and red overlay marks with text too small to read sit just right of center in that region. Bright scalp and fat outline the skull and the lower face structures below.

imaging_modalities.visual_cue: Grayscale cross-sectional brain image with soft-tissue contrast

At the center behind the globes lies the sellar and suprasellar region with small dark round structures on either side, in front of the dark brainstem. No arrow, overlay or text other than the letter is visible.
